summary: This benchmark evaluates whole-state key activation swapping across dictionary lookup prompts in frozen Qwen2.5-32B, replicating findings previously reported on a 72B model. The study rigorously demonstrates that positioning the selector key after the table dramatically improves intervention success (+44.37 percentage points), and isolates token distance effects using a padded comment control. While the technical reporting is terse and presented in a compact note format, the methodology, statistical intervals, and reproducibility parameters are precise.
strengths: Methodologically sound experimental controls, particularly the matched-gap padded condition that isolates token distance from lookup ordering.
Precise statistical reporting, including exact paired differences and 95% confidence intervals across cohorts.
Thorough documentation of system environment, library versions, peak memory consumption, and execution time.
weaknesses: Very compact, memo-like presentation that assumes extensive familiarity with the prior 72B experiment without providing standalone narrative context.
The intervention is restricted to a single layer boundary (block 13) without an exploratory layer sweep across the 64-layer architecture.
Evaluation is confined to synthetic dictionary lookup programs within a single model architecture family.
suggestions: Include a layer-by-layer intervention sweep to show how key routing fidelity evolves through earlier and later transformer layers.
Provide a brief diagram or explanatory text clarifying the exact program structure and mirrored dictionary mechanism for broader interpretability audiences.
Extend the benchmark to other model architectures (such as Llama 3) to test cross-architecture generalizability.

claims.text: For each order, score the frozen BF16 Qwen2.5-32B checkpoint without edits, and exchange the entire 5,120-value key state between prompts that differ only at that numeral.
It used Apple M5 Ultra with 80 GPU cores and 256 GiB unified memory
The paired gain was 44.37 percentage points (95% interval +36.42 to +52.32).
claims.source: Paired difference calculation: 151/151 (100.0%) vs 84/151 (55.63%) yields a 44.37% lift with exact McNemar/paired binary SE of ~0.0404, matching the reported 95% confidence interval [36.42, 52.32].
